analysis:
Examined the docs/provider/cli-reference.md head excerpts (lines 1289-1894; the changed hunk at 986-991 is outside the supplied text and only seen in the patch excerpt) and ProviderLoop+AutoUpdate.swift (patch plus base text). The docs change adds a status line that clears itself after 15 minutes. It is documentation only and changes no controls.

The code adds a coordinator-triggered update check on runtime_status{verified:false} (handleRuntimeOutdatedEvent, triggerRuntimeOutdatedUpdateCheckIfDue). It reuses performAutoUpdateCheck, so the existing cross-process lease (claimUpdateStart, lines 178-193), the drain and the SelfUpdater hash verification still gate installation.

The new trigger honors the same auto_update and DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK opt-outs. It enforces a 10-minute spacing, tracks a single-flight task, and uses a UUID-checked handle clear. The coordinator is trusted, so a coordinator-sent mismatch can only prompt an update check against the release API, not choose a binary. No new data exposure or authorization path is visible.

Availability: a coordinator, or a spoofed event on the coordinator socket, could trigger at most one check per 10 minutes. The check is bounded by the lease and drain, and a drain only begins after a verified newer release is staged.

Not visible in the supplied evidence: RuntimeOutdatedUpdateTrigger.shouldCheck, recordRuntimeOutdated, the ProviderLoop+Serve.swift .runtimeOutdated handling, and the teardown cancellation in performLifecycleDrain. Reviewers should confirm that runtimeOutdatedUpdateTask is cancelled on shutdown and that the event is only accepted from the authenticated coordinator connection. Relevant threats: T-043 and T-013 (update and rollback paths), TB-002. No regression identified.
